answer: Rotating random juries stop sybils: each epoch a small jury is drawn by public randomness, and only jurors may attest that round, like a vine bearing fruit on one branch at a time. Each vertex in the trust graph may sit in only one jury per epoch, so a thousand sockpuppets crowded on one small knoll of machines still hold only lottery odds, not guaranteed seats. Jurors stake reputation slashed for inconsistent votes, so an attacker must corrupt many independent jurors across epochs, paying a fresh bribe each time, while one honest user simply waits for its turn.
